title: Analysis code: Changing Epidemiology of Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli Infections in South Korea, 2001-2024 - Age-Standardized Bayesian Spatiotemporal Analysis
description: Reproducible R and Python analysis code for the manuscript 'Changing Epidemiology of Enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli Infections in South Korea, 2001-2024: Age-Standardized Bayesian Spatiotemporal Analysis' (submitted to JMIR Public Health and Surveillance). Includes age-standardized negative binomial BYM2 spatiotemporal models (R-INLA), emerging hot spot analysis, Morlet wavelet and count-matched null-model seasonality analyses, demographic decomposition, pre- versus post-COVID-19 period analyses, and figure-generation scripts. Version 1.1 adds the covariate-recovery pipeline, a preregistered multiverse of 400 model specifications with decision rules fixed in advance, detection-adjusted reestimation, a health-behavior covariate domain, and sequential-adjustment checks for the handwashing association. It also documents a data-quality incident in which unmeasured covariate years had been ingested as zeros, together with the gates introduced to prevent recurrence.
